summary:
Centered on Jezero Crater, it combines spacecraft observations, geological research, route planning, and human exploration models to demonstrate how Martian terrain affects astronaut mobility and mission decisions.

Using NASA and USGS elevation data and orbital imagery, the simulator covers approximately 373 km² of regional terrain, with a detailed HiRISE view of the landing area. Users can explore elevation, slope, potential hazards, scientific sites, sample-collection locations, 15 mapped bedrock units, and surface-cover types such as sand, talus, and mantling deposits.

An A* route-planning algorithm enables users to select destinations, mark avoid zones, and compare routes based on terrain accessibility, estimated astronaut energy expenditure, and scientific value, including mapped geological contacts. Route summaries display distance, estimated walking time, metabolic energy, and relative terrain risk.

Users can explore through an animated third-person astronaut or a NASA Perseverance rover model. Terrain-dependent movement and visual effects simulate wheel slipping, settling, steering, dust, and tracks. Automatic travel follows selected routes and displays movement commands, estimated power, accumulated energy use, and remaining distance, with pause, resume, and manual control options.
details:
Human-Centered Route Planning

Mars Explorer goes beyond conventional shortest-path navigation by considering the challenges of human exploration. Its route planner evaluates multiple factors, including terrain accessibility, slope, potential hazards, physical workload, and scientific value.

Users can compare alternative routes and identify paths that balance astronaut safety with opportunities for meaningful scientific investigation.

Terrain and Geological Analysis

The platform combines planetary elevation data, orbital imagery, and geological information to provide an interactive view of Jezero Crater.

Key features include:

  • Elevation and slope visualization
  • Potential terrain hazards
  • 15 mapped bedrock units
  • Surface-cover categories, including sand, talus, and mantling deposits
  • Geological contacts and scientific exploration sites
  • Sample-collection locations

These layers help users understand the geological context of potential exploration areas and evaluate how different surface conditions may affect mobility.

Astronaut Mobility and Energy Estimation

Mars Explorer considers the physical demands of traversing different Martian terrains. Route summaries include estimated walking time and metabolic energy expenditure, while the optional Marswalk model explores additional factors such as oxygen consumption, heat storage, scientific workload, and return reserves.

These estimates use configurable assumptions and illustrative simulation models rather than representing validated measurements of actual astronaut performance.

Interactive Exploration Simulation

Users can explore the terrain through an animated third-person astronaut or a NASA Perseverance rover model. Terrain-dependent movement and visual effects help demonstrate how surface conditions can influence navigation.

The automatic travel mode follows a selected route while displaying movement commands, estimated power, accumulated energy use, and remaining distance. Users can pause, resume, or take manual control at any time.

Scientific and Educational Context

Educational field notes introduce Jezero Crater's geological history, past habitability, and potential biosignatures while distinguishing scientific evidence from confirmed discoveries.

By combining geological context, terrain analysis, mobility estimation, and scientific priorities, Mars Explorer turns planetary exploration planning into an interactive learning experience.

What Makes Mars Explorer Different?

Rather than optimizing routes solely by distance, Mars Explorer adopts a human-centered, multi-criteria approach to Martian exploration. It connects terrain safety, astronaut mobility, estimated physical workload, and scientific exploration value within a single interactive environment.

The platform aims to help users understand not only where astronauts can travel, but also how difficult the journey may be and what scientific opportunities they may encounter along the way.
